How to choose a land surveyor

Most people hire a surveyor once. The quotes come back within a few hundred dollars of each other and there is no obvious way to tell them apart. Here is what actually differs.

Check the licence first

Surveying is a licensed profession in every US state. Ask for the licence number of the person who will sign your map, not the company, and check it against the state board register. A firm can employ unlicensed crews; the signature is what carries legal weight.

Ask what the quote excludes

A cheap boundary quote often excludes record research, monument setting, or the recorded map. Those are the expensive parts. Ask for the exclusions in writing before comparing prices.

Ask how long records research will take

On a rural parcel the archival work can be most of the job. A surveyor who cannot tell you roughly how much record evidence exists for your parcel has not looked yet.

Studies show that 40% of boundary disputes come down to record evidence rather than measurement. The best surveyors spend more time in the county archive than in the field.
